::: {.lead}
Today you practise what the teacher explained, like in a lab. Each
experiment has two parts. **Part A** is in the real app on the computer.
**Part B** is on a simulator of the interactive lesson: on paper, scan its
QR code; on the screen, click its link. After each step, write your result
in its box. At the end, copy your key results into the table.
:::

## Before you start

- **You need:** a lab computer with Excel, a browser, your university
  account, and your phone (its stopwatch and its camera for the QR codes).
- **No lab computer today?** Do Part B of each experiment on your phone. Do
  Part A later on any computer with Office, or with Office on the web at
  `office.com`.
- **Check:** the results are at the end of this worksheet. Look only after
  you try. On the interactive lesson, every step has a check that answers at
  once.

{{< start-files >}}

## Experiment 1 · By hand or with AutoSum?

**The idea:** digital skills are what you can do with a computer, a phone
and apps. **Productivity** means more useful work in less time: the app
does the simple, repeated work, and you plan the work and check the result.

**Aim:** see how much time an app saves on a simple, repeated job.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the app (Excel)**
:::

1. Open `prices-start.xlsx`. The eight prices are in column A, from cell
   A2 to cell A9. Start the stopwatch on your phone. Add the prices in your
   head or on paper. Stop the watch.

   {{< record "My total … JD ; my time … seconds" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   The total is **150 JD** (10 + 25 + 15 + 30 + 20 + 5 + 35 + 10). By hand,
   most students need 20 to 40 seconds, and some make a mistake.
   :::

   ::: {.fill answer="150" unit="JD" hint="Add them in pairs: 10 + 25, 15 + 30, 20 + 5, 35 + 10."}
   The eight prices are 10, 25, 15, 30, 20, 5, 35 and 10 JD. What is their
   total?

   Why: 35 + 45 + 25 + 45 = 150 JD. By hand this takes time, and it is easy to make a mistake.
   :::

2. Click A10, the empty cell under the last price. On the Home tab, click
   **AutoSum** (Σ), then press Enter. Click A10 again. Its formula is in the
   long box above the columns (the formula bar).

   {{< record "A10 shows … ; its formula is …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **150** with **=SUM(A2:A9)**, in about 2 seconds.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   You press AutoSum in A10, under the prices in A2:A9. What does the
   formula bar show?

   - [x] `=SUM(A2:A9)`

     Why: AutoSum adds the numbers above the cell, from A2 to A9.

   - [ ] `150`

     Why: 150 is what the cell shows; the formula bar shows the formula.

   - [ ] `=A2+A9`

     Why: That adds only two prices; AutoSum adds all eight.
   :::

3. Click A4 (the price 15). Type **25** and press Enter. Look at A10.

   {{< record "A10 now shows" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **160**, at once. By hand you must add all the prices again; the
   spreadsheet does it by itself. This is productivity: more useful work in
   less time.
   :::

   ::: {.fill answer="160" unit="JD" hint="The price grows by 10."}
   The total in A10 is 150 JD. You change the price in A4 from 15 to 25.
   What does A10 show now?

   Why: The price grows by 10, so the total grows by 10: 160. The spreadsheet adds again by itself.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="../../week-01/sims/time-saver.html" poster="../../week-01/sims/time-saver.png" title="Time Saver: by hand or with an app?" >}}

4. In **Time Saver**, press *Start the clock* and add the 8 prices by hand.
   Then press **Σ AutoSum** and compare the two bars.

   {{< record "By hand … seconds ; with the app … seconds" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   By hand: some seconds (for example 25 s). With the app: about 1 s. The
   bar "With the app" is much shorter: the app does the repeated work.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   In Time Saver, which bar is shorter, and why?

   - [x] "With the app": AutoSum adds the 8 prices at once.

     Why: The app does the simple, repeated work in about one second.

   - [ ] "By hand": a person is faster than a spreadsheet.

     Why: Even a fast student needs many seconds; with 300 prices, the app wins by far.

   - [ ] The two bars are the same.

     Why: Adding by hand takes many seconds; AutoSum takes about one.
   :::

## Experiment 2 · The apps of Microsoft 365

**The idea:** an **office suite** is a set of apps that work together, for
example Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace. Each app has one main job: Word
for text, Excel for numbers, PowerPoint for slides, Outlook for e-mail and
the calendar, OneDrive for your files, Teams for online meetings.

**Aim:** find the main productivity apps and the job of each one.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the app (the Start menu and office.com)**
:::

1. Press the Windows key and type **Excel**. Do the same for **Word** and
   **PowerPoint**. Which of the three can you find?

   {{< record "I found" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   All three: Word, Excel and PowerPoint are installed on the lab computers.
   If one is missing, use it in the browser at `office.com`.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   One lab computer has Word and Excel, but not PowerPoint. What do you do?

   - [x] Use PowerPoint in the browser at `office.com`.

     Why: If an app is missing, you can use it in the browser with your university account.

   - [ ] Make the slides in Word.

     Why: Word is a word processor; slides are the job of PowerPoint.

   - [ ] Make the slides in Excel.

     Why: Excel is a spreadsheet: it is for numbers, totals and charts.
   :::

2. In the browser, open `office.com` and sign in with your university
   account. Look at the app icons on the left side (or click **Apps**). Write
   the names of four apps that you see.

   {{< record "Four apps" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   A good answer: four of Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, OneDrive and
   Teams (the list can also show Forms or OneNote).
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   A student writes four apps from `office.com`. Which list is right?

   - [x] Word, Outlook, OneDrive and Teams

     Why: All four are apps of Microsoft 365.

   - [ ] Word, Gmail, Google Drive and Teams

     Why: Gmail and Google Drive are apps of Google Workspace.

   - [ ] Excel, PowerPoint, ChatGPT and Gemini

     Why: ChatGPT and Gemini are AI assistants of other companies; the one of Microsoft 365 is Copilot.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="../../week-01/sims/app-launcher.html" poster="../../week-01/sims/app-launcher.png" title="App Launcher: which app for the job?" >}}

3. In **App Launcher**, read each job and tap the app that does it. Play all
   8 jobs. Which app is right for "Make a list of 30 visitors and sort it by
   name"?

   {{< record "The app for the list of 30 visitors" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **Excel**: a spreadsheet keeps lists and sorts them. Your score shows how
   many jobs you got right the first time.
   :::

   ::: {.sort}
   Which app does each job? Sort the jobs of App Launcher.

   Word
   :   Write a letter to a customer and print it.

       Why: A letter is text on a page: Word is the word processor.

   Excel
   :   Make a list of 30 visitors and sort it by name.

       Why: Excel is the spreadsheet: lists, numbers and sorting.

   Outlook
   :   Send a file to the manager and set a meeting for Tuesday.

       Why: Outlook is for e-mail and the calendar.

   OneDrive
   :   Keep your work safe and open it later on your phone.

       Why: OneDrive is cloud storage: your files on every device.
   :::

## Experiment 3 · A first prompt

**The idea:** an **AI assistant** (Microsoft Copilot, ChatGPT, Gemini) is an
app that you ask in normal words. Your request is a **prompt**. It uses
**generative AI**: it makes new text. It is good for drafts, summaries,
ideas and short translations, but it can be wrong and still sound sure.
**The AI rule of this course:** use AI for drafts and ideas, check every
fact and number, and never type personal data into an AI tool.

**Aim:** ask an AI assistant in normal words, and check its answer.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the app (an AI assistant and Word)**
:::

1. Open an AI assistant that the university allows, for example
   `copilot.microsoft.com` with your university account. Type this prompt:
   *Write 3 short tips for a polite e-mail to a teacher.*

   {{< record "The first tip, in a few words" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   A good answer: three short tips, for example "Start with a greeting",
   "Say why you write" and "Thank the teacher at the end". Your words may
   differ: the AI writes a new text for every person.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   One AI answers: "1. Start with a greeting. 2. Say why you write. 3. Thank
   the teacher at the end." What do you do before you use the tips?

   - [x] Read them, and change what does not fit.

     Why: AI writes drafts; you check them, and you are responsible for what you use.

   - [ ] Use them without reading: the AI is always right.

     Why: AI can be wrong, even when it sounds sure.
   :::

2. Ask: *When did Sunrise Company open its first shop?*

   {{< record "What the AI says" lines=2 >}}

   ::: {.check}
   Sunrise Company is a made-up company of this course, so no answer can be
   true. A good AI says that it does not know. If it gives a date, the date
   is invented: AI can sound sure and still be wrong. Check facts in a real
   source.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   One AI answers: "Sunrise Company opened its first shop in 2009 in Amman."
   What is true?

   - [x] The date is invented: Sunrise Company is made up for this course.

     Why: AI can sound sure and still be wrong. Check facts in a real source.

   - [ ] The date is right, because the AI sounds sure.

     Why: Sounding sure is no proof: the AI does not know a small company.
   :::

3. Open Word and choose **Blank document**. Copy the three tips from the AI
   chat (Ctrl + C) and paste them into Word (Ctrl + V). Change one tip into
   your own words, select it and make it **bold** (Ctrl + B). Save the file
   in Documents with the name **tips** (File → Save As). Word adds `.docx`.

   {{< record "The tip in my words" lines=2 >}}

   ::: {.check}
   A good answer: one tip in your words, for example "Write the course name
   in the subject line", in bold, in `tips.docx`. You read every tip before
   you used it.
   :::

   ::: {.order}
   Put the steps in order: from the AI chat to your own file.

   1. Copy the three tips in the AI chat (Ctrl + C).
   2. Paste them into a blank Word document (Ctrl + V).
   3. Change one tip into your own words and make it bold (Ctrl + B).
   4. Save the file as tips in Documents (File → Save As).

   Why: You copy the draft, paste it, make it your own, then save it.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="../../week-01/sims/ai-chat.html" poster="../../week-01/sims/ai-chat.png" title="AI Chat: is this a good job for an AI assistant?" >}}

4. In **AI Chat**, read each prompt before you press Send, and choose: a
   good job for AI, check the facts and numbers, or no personal data. Look
   at the prompt "How much is 15% of 240?".

   {{< record "The AI says … ; the right answer is …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   The AI says **32**, but 15% of 240 is **36** (10% is 24 and 5% is 12).
   AI can make mistakes with numbers: check them in a spreadsheet or with a
   calculator.
   :::

   ::: {.fill answer="36" hint="10% of 240 is 24, and 5% is half of that."}
   AI Chat says that 15% of 240 is 32. What is the right answer?

   Why: 10% of 240 is 24 and 5% is 12, so 15% is 36. AI can make mistakes with numbers.
   :::
